Hi Samantha — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment on the hosting mode and network asks.

Summary of your preferences from the call:
- FinEdge prefers private VPC (PrivateBridge) for initial production due to regulatory needs and separation between environments.
- You want Redwood Private running in your VPC via PrivateLink if possible, but are open to VPC peering if there are constraints.
- Timeline: target pilot in Q2 with a locked-down egress allowlist for production.

Concrete asks from our side:
1) Can you confirm whether your network team prefers PrivateLink or VPC peering (we can support both)? If undecided, we will propose PrivateLink as the default for least blast radius.
2) Please provide the egress IP ranges we should allowlist (or tell us who on your network team we should work with).
3) Attached is our minimal networking template (redwood_privatenet_template.csv) — please fill the highlighted rows and return.

Next steps I propose:
- You to confirm a preferred connectivity pattern and provide contact for network/infra ops (Eric?).
- JD from our side (Jordan) will follow up with an exact port list, cert fingerprint requirements, and PrivateLink ARN examples.

I’ll keep this thread as the single place for technical attachments and the network inventory.

Thanks,
Jonas Weber

Hi team — quick technical checklist from the infra/ops side (keeping it terse for Eric):

1) PrivateLink approach (recommended):
   - We will supply the Service Name and the expected VPC Endpoint Service configuration (AWS NLB-backed).
   - Customer must create an Interface VPC Endpoint in the desired FinEdge VPC and accept the endpoint connection.

2) Allowlist / egress expectations:
   - Outbound from FinEdge to Redwood (if any) — not required for PrivateLink because traffic enters via interface endpoints.
   - Redwood egress that FinEdge may need to allow (for certain telemetry or 3rd-party callbacks): 34.210.45.32/28 (Redwood monitoring), 54.85.12.0/26 (metrics ingestion). We will keep that list short and update with any final surprises.

3) Ports & TLS:
   - TCP 443 only for application traffic to the PrivateLink endpoint.
   - We terminate TLS on our side; we do not require mutual TLS for the initial pilot. If FinEdge needs mTLS we can enable in a later rollout.

4) Certificate / SNI expectations:
   - SNI will be present; no certificate pinning required. We will share the SAN names to expect (redwood-privatenet.redwood.ai).

5) Handover items we need from FinEdge:
   - Interface endpoint acceptance contact and timeline (Eric).
   - Confirm admin CIDR of the subnet where the interface endpoint will be created.
   - Completed redwood_privatenet_template.csv with VLAN IDs / NAT ranges (Jonas noted this).

I’ve attached a short internal runbook excerpt for the team (pasted below). If Eric or Samantha want a short 20–30 min ops-to-ops call, we can do that next week.

-- Jordan Blake
